en: PHIVOLCS monitors Taal Volcano to warn residents about dangerous ashfall and toxic gases before they cause harm.
PAGASA issues color-coded rain warnings to tell students exactly when heavy floods make traveling to school unsafe.
The active Valley Fault System crosses Metro Manila, so families must prepare earthquake emergency kits to survive tremors.
The highly polluted Marilao River in Bulacan contains toxic heavy metals, making its water unsafe for swimming or drinking.
High heat index levels during the Philippine dry season cause heat stroke, so students must drink plenty of water.
Stagnant rainwater in empty tires breeds Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which spread dangerous dengue fever throughout Philippine neighborhoods.
The intense tropical sunlight at Boracay beach emits strong ultraviolet rays that cause sunburns without proper sunscreen protection.
Heavy vehicle traffic along EDSA releases harmful exhaust fumes, so wearing a mask helps protect your lungs from pollution.
Continuous heavy rains in the steep Cordillera mountains trigger deadly landslides, requiring residents to quickly evacuate to safer ground.
Swimming in the heavily polluted waters of Laguna de Bay can expose you to harmful bacteria and skin infections.
The Bureau of Fisheries bans shellfish harvesting in Manila Bay during red tide to prevent deadly paralytic shellfish poisoning.
The highly venomous Philippine cobra hides in the leaf litter of Mount Makiling, so hikers must wear closed shoes.
